title: Aran-weight striped baby blanket
subtitle: A fast two-colour baby blanket in garter stripes at aran weight.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in two-colour garter stripes worked at aran weight on 5 mm needles. Aran yarn knits faster than DK and produces a warmer blanket; about 150 g of each colour. The stripe sequence carries both yarns up the side edge.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 7th series (1891), §Aran Weight Baby Wraps, lists aran-weight garter baby blankets with stripe sequences as standard nursery items. The carry-up-the-side technique for alternating colours is described in the same source under §Striped Knitting.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 36 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn weight class equivalent to CYC 4 (medium), knitting to approximately 16 to 20 stitches per 10 cm on 4.5 to 5.5 mm needles. Called aran weight in the UK because it corresponds to the yarn traditionally used for Aran-patterned sweaters; called worsted in the US.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat in garter-stitch stripes on 5 mm needles using
aran-weight
yarn in two colours, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction needs no seaming. Aran weight was chosen over DK because it produces a warmer blanket at fewer rows: at this gauge the blanket needs about 324 rows instead of around 396 rows in DK, which represents a material saving in knitting time. Two colours in four-row garter stripes carry neatly up the left edge without cutting, keeping ends to just four total. Budget about 150 g of each colour (roughly 270 m / 295 yards per colour) of superwash aran. Buy all the yarn in matched dye lots. Drapes across a cot end or folds for a pram bag.
What you need

items.name: Yarn A
items.qty: 150 g (about 270 m / 295 yards) of aran-weight machine-washable yarn

items.name: Yarn B
items.qty: 150 g (about 270 m / 295 yards) of the same aran yarn in a contrasting or complementary colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 5 mm needles, unblocked. Swatch one colour only; the stripe does not affect gauge. Work a 15 cm square swatch and measure the centre 10 cm after leaving it flat overnight.
If your gauge is 16 stitches per 10 cm with a 135-stitch cast-on, the blanket will be about 84 cm wide instead of 75 cm. Adjust the cast-on to an even number for the target width.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using Yarn A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 135 stitches. Long-tail tail: (5 × 135) / 10 + 15 = 67.5 + 15 = 83 cm. Measure 95 cm of tail.
Stripe sequence
Rows 1 to 4: using Yarn A, knit every row.
Rows 5 to 8: pick up Yarn B at the left edge, leaving a 10 cm tail on the first use. Knit every row with Yarn B. Twist Yarn A loosely at the left edge on rows 5 and 7 to carry it up the side.
Repeat the 8-row sequence until the blanket measures 90 cm. Always change colour at the same edge. When you set this aside, note the current row within the stripe and which yarn is at the needle.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 162 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 135 stitches. At row 322 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Carried yarn pulling in the side edge: the twist at the edge was too tight. Twist the carried yarn loosely; it only needs to be anchored, not pulled.

Aran-weight join visible at the stripe edge: the first stitch of each new colour is noticeably looser than the rest. Snug the first stitch of each colour firmly before continuing. Aran-weight yarn makes colour joins more visible than DK because the stitches are larger.
Dye-lot shift within one colour partway through: skeins of the same colour from different lots were not alternated. Switch to alternating skeins every two rows when moving between lots.
Cast-off
Using whichever colour is at the needle when the blanket reaches 90 cm, cast off knitwise with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in all four ends on the wrong side, running each tail 5 cm along a garter ridge and changing direction once. Aran-weight tails weave in quickly because each ridge is thick.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle if superwash aran. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

Once two-colour aran stripes are easy, try a cable panel baby blanket: the same aran weight and 5 mm needles but with a central cable column flanked by seed-stitch panels on each side. The cable panel is the main skill step; the blanket width and cast-on are the same.
